purpose: The wire between Rock and the chat platform. The column lists are the positional order of the sync payload rows, the enum value lists are what each side mirrors as a typed vocabulary, the headers are what a submission carries, the push is the key set of an immediate push body, the claim names are what a person token carries, and the error codes are the one vocabulary every layer branches on. Generated from the database the migrations produce; never edited by hand.
hash_recipe: SHA-256, lowercase hex, over the UTF-8 bytes of one line per table in the order the tables array gives: the table name, a colon, the wire column names joined by commas, each line closed by a line feed. The JSON is deliberately not what is hashed, so no key order, whitespace or string escaping rule has to be agreed between the languages that compute it. The hash covers the column lists and nothing else: it is compared at ingest, so anything it covered would refuse every submission from every church still on the previous Rock build the moment it changed, and an added enum value is meant to ship to the platform first and leave those churches working.

submit_headers.name: x-sync-submission-id
submit_headers.carries: A uuid generated in Rock, the idempotency key for this submission.

submit_headers.name: x-sync-read-at
submit_headers.carries: The UTC time taken in Rock before the projection read, truncated to microseconds, written as ISO 8601 with an explicit offset (Z or +hh:mm) and at most six fractional digits; any other form is refused. It is the clock every row of this payload is judged by, and it is Rock's clock, never the platform's.

submit_headers.name: x-sync-counts
submit_headers.carries: An object with exactly the four keys listed above and the expected row count of each, so a truncated read cannot pass as a small payload. The keys are the short names of the four payload sections, the same four the payload itself is keyed by, and they are deliberately not the table names: build this header from the tables array below and every submission is refused. They carry no order, because neither this header nor the payload is a list.

submit_headers.name: x-sync-marks
submit_headers.carries: The identity high-water value of the four Rock tables the projection reads, as an object with exactly the four keys listed above and a whole number each. It is the identity seed rather than the maximum id, because the maximum drops when the newest rows are deleted and the seed does not. The platform keeps the highest it has seen and refuses a submission whose marks moved backwards, which is what a restored database does and ordinary operation does not.

submit_headers.name: x-sync-rock-version
submit_headers.carries: The version of Rock that produced this payload, recorded with the submission.

submit_headers.name: x-sync-contract
submit_headers.carries: The wire hash below. Compared at ingest against the platform's own value, which is the only check that can see a same-width column reorder; the row width check cannot.

submit_headers.name: x-sync-urgent
submit_headers.carries: The value 1 for a manual sync and for a failed immediate write that needs draining sooner. Never set for a first load. Absent, or any other value, means ordinary priority, which is why this is the one optional header.

payload.carries: The body of a submission: one object with exactly these four keys, each holding an array of positional rows for the table of the same position in the tables array below. A row is an array of that table wire column values, in the order the column list gives and nothing else. Absent from an array means absent from the church, which is what makes a restatement a statement of existence rather than a set of changes.

empty_sections.reason: A badge changes only when the church edits its badge settings or a Data View persists, and neither is a save the immediate sync sees, so badges travel in the full restatement alone and a push that carries a badge row is refused.

absent.carries: An object with exactly the sets listed here, each an array of keys. A push is never a restatement, so a row it does not mention is left as it is, and only a key listed here is stamped absent. A key both carried in a section and listed here is refused, since one push is one statement of truth at one time.

sets.name: channels
sets.carries: Each channel Rock asked about that is no longer a chat channel, or no longer exists.

sets.name: members
sets.carries: Each membership Rock asked about that is no longer live, keyed by the channel and the person's primary alias, the same alias the membership row carries.

push.carries: The body of an immediate push: one JSON object with exactly the four sections, positional rows as a submission carries them, and the absent key below. It is sent with the read-time and contract headers a submission carries, and the rows are applied under the same row clock.

not_on_the_wire.reason: The church comes from the credential the submission is made with. No function anywhere accepts a tenant from its caller, so a payload that could name its own tenant would be the one way one church could write another church's rows.
